lessons.title: をおいて～ない (wo oite ~ nai)
lessons.meaning: except for ~, there is no ...; no one/nothing other than ~
lessons.explanation: Expresses “no one/nothing but …” (the only exception/choice). Often used in written or formal style: Nをおいて～ない.

examples.jp: 彼(かれ)をおいて、この仕事(しごと)を任(まか)せられる人(ひと)はいない。
examples.romaji: kare o oite, kono shigoto o makaserareru hito wa inai.
examples.en: There is no one other than him whom I can entrust with this job.

examples.jp: 君(きみ)をおいて、そんな相談(そうだん)ができる相手(あいて)はいない。
examples.romaji: kimi o oite, sonna soudan ga dekiru aite wa inai.
examples.en: Other than you, there is no one I can talk to about something like that.

examples.jp: この町(まち)をおいて、こんなに静(しず)かな場所(ばしょ)はない。
examples.romaji: kono machi o oite, konnani shizukana basho wa nai.
examples.en: There is no place as quiet as this town.

quiz.question_jp: 彼(かれ)(　)、この役(やく)を演(えん)じられる俳優(はいゆう)はいない。
quiz.question_en: Choose the grammar pattern that best completes the sentence.
quiz.source_sentence_jp: 彼(かれ)をおいて、この役(やく)を演(えん)じられる俳優(はいゆう)はいない。

quiz.question_jp: 「彼(かれ)をおいて、この仕事(しごと)を任(まか)せられる人(ひと)はいない。」の意味(いみ)として最(もっと)も近(ちか)いものはどれですか。
quiz.question_en: Which meaning is the closest?
choices: He is not suitable for the job.
Only he can be entrusted with this job.
He refused to do the job.
Many people can do this job better than him.
quiz.answer: Only he can be entrusted with this job.
choices_raw: He is not suitable for the job.
Only he can be entrusted with this job.

quiz.answer_raw: Only he can be entrusted with this job.

quiz.question_en: Choose the grammar pattern that best completes the sentence.

lessons.title: というより (to iu yori)
lessons.meaning: rather than; more like; instead of saying ~
lessons.explanation: Used to correct/soften a statement: AというよりB (“not so much A as B / rather than A, more like B”).

examples.jp: 青(あお)というより、紫(むらさき)だね。
examples.romaji: ao to iu yori, murasaki da ne.
examples.en: It's more purple than blue.

examples.jp: 休憩(きゅうけい)というより、ただのサボりだ。
examples.romaji: kyuukei to iu yori, tada no sabori da.
examples.en: Rather than a break, it's just slacking off.

examples.jp: 驚(おどろ)いたというより、あきれた。
examples.romaji: odoroita to iu yori, akireta.
examples.en: More than surprised, I was taken aback.

choices: I was more taken aback than surprised.

lessons.title: あくまでも (akumade mo)
lessons.meaning: to the end; persistently; absolutely; is still very ~
lessons.explanation: あくまでも means “to the end / stubbornly / absolutely”. It emphasizes that something does not change: あくまでもNだ.

examples.jp: 空(そら)はあくまでも青(あお)い。
examples.romaji: sora wa akumade mo aoi.
examples.en: The sky is as blue as blue can be.

examples.jp: あくまでも見積(みつ)もりです。
examples.romaji: akumade mo mitsumori desu.
examples.en: It's only an estimate.

examples.jp: あくまでも個人(こじん)の感想(かんそう)です。
examples.romaji: akumade mo kojin no kansou desu.
examples.en: It is nothing more than an individual's opinion.

lessons.title: あっての (atte no)
lessons.meaning: which can exist solely due to the presence of; which owes everything to
lessons.explanation: あっての means “only because of / it is thanks to … that … exists”. Pattern: NあってのN.

examples.en: I know you're complaining about your car being totaled but it's just a good thing you weren't injured. You should be thankful to be alive.

lessons.title: ならでは (nara dewa)
lessons.meaning: distinctive of; uniquely applying to; special to ~
lessons.explanation: ならでは expresses something unique/characteristic to a person, place, or thing: Nならでは(の)N / Nならではだ.

examples.jp: 観光(かんこう)地(ち)では地元(じもと)ならではのものを食(た)べたい。
examples.romaji: kankou chi de wa jimotonarade wa no mono o tabetai.
examples.en: I want to eat some local food where we're sightseeing.

examples.jp: 田舎(いなか)は何(なん)かと不便(ふべん)ですが、田舎(いなか)ならではの良(よ)さもたくさんあります。
examples.romaji: inaka wa nan ka to fuben desu ga, inakanarade wa no yo sa mo takusan arimasu.
examples.en: The countryside is inconvenient, but it has many advantages that you will find nowhere else.

examples.jp: 「昨夜(さくや)、遅(おそ)くまでごそごそしてたわね。何時(いつ)に寝(ね)たの？」「五(ご)時(じ)。だって、前(まえ)の日(ひ)に麻雀(まーじゃん)しててさぁ、寝(ね)たのが明け方(あけがた)で起(お)きたの夕方(ゆうがた)の５時(じ)過(す)ぎだったんだよ。寝(ね)れなくて」「なるほどね、朝日(あさひ)と共(とも)に寝(ね)て、夕日(ゆうひ)と共(とも)に起(お)きるってことね。大学(だいがく)生(せい)ならではだよね」。
examples.romaji: 「 sakuya, osoku made gosogoso shiteta wa ne. itsu ni neta no? 」 「 go ji. da tte, mae no hi ni maajan shitete saa, neta no ga akegata de okita no yuugata no ５ ji sugidattan da yo. nerenakute 」 「 naruhodo ne, asahi to tomo ni nete, yuuhi to tomo ni okiru tte koto ne. daigaku seinarade wa da yo ne 」.
examples.en: "You were fumbling about until late last night, weren't you? What time did you go to bed?" "Five o'clock. It's because I was playing mahjong the day before. I went to sleep at dawn and got up at 5 in the evening. I couldn't sleep during the night." "I see. So going to sleep with the rising sun and waking with the setting sun. Something you'd only find a university student doing."
